chapter: Reel two to four: pay, tailgate and style
title: How the name Mr. Tailgate came about, and playing on wagons
summary: He explains tailgate trombone from advertising wagons where the slide needed room, and says the nickname stuck; they recall bumpy wagon rides.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What about, how did you get that name, Mr. Tailgate, I wanted to ask you.

Well, you see, you know the funny thing, I had a club in Baton Rouge, and I named it the Tailgate Club. And two ladies came there and said, could you tell me what you mean by tailgate? I said, alright. I said, you see, when I was a kid, we used to valley-hoo on a wagon, so the trombone probably couldn't get inside the wagon. They had the drums and all that stuff and they didn't have room to slide these slides. Because on the outside had signs on both sides, see, so you didn't have room to slide. So they put you on a tailgate. See, the bass player and the trombones sat on the tailgate. Well, they had plenty of room to slide. That's why it said tailgate trombone. That's what it was.

But who put the name on you? Huh? Who gave you the name, Mr. Tailgate? Well, I don't know how that happened, see. Well, it's been a long time. Oh, yeah, gee. At least 20 years, or more than that. Oh, more than that, yeah.

And I think I overheard somebody say that the trombone sits on a tailgate, see. And a lot of people ask me that all the time, we're on a club. Where did you get the name tailgate? So I explained them. You sit on a tailgate when you play. It's the only place you have room. Just like the bass fiddle used to. Boy, that was a hell of a thing. Sometimes you had some bad horses, you know.
It would knock you right out of the wagon, see. It could break your heart. Well, break everything. Breeding your lips and everything. Break your mouth and everything.
Yeah. Did you play while the wagon was moving?
Oh, yeah, sometimes, sure. But we used to go on corners, barns, you know, and play all those corners. Just like you see a lot of these colored bands, let alone all these wagons. Yeah.
